question: Does anonymous structural context predict which operator occurs next, beyond operator frequency and prefix-position effects, in Hebrew and glyph corpora independently; and do anonymous states show aligned operator-selection strength across systems without pairing operator identities?
claimBoundary: A positive Hebrew result supports a structural operator-selection grammar under the frozen anonymous four-history projector. A positive cross-system result supports alignment of state-level selection strength only; it does not identify Hebrew operators with glyphs or prove common origin. Failure rejects only this local operator-selection test.

lineage.motivation: V20-V27 repeatedly show real operator and context information but local context-by-operator consequence interactions fail. V28 reverses direction and tests whether context selects the operator rather than modifies its consequence.

hebrewSplit.assignment: Sort canonical book osisIDs by sha256(salt + ':' + book). Assign rank modulo 5: residues 0,1,2 TRAIN; 3 holdout; 4 control.

projector.state: anonymous equality pattern of the previous four identities in the same representation, padded by <START>; current operator is excluded
projector.positionBucket: prefix token count i bucketed as 0,1,2,3,4,5-7,8-11,12-15,16-23,24+

models.primaryGain: log2 Psel(actual O|S0,pos) - log2 Ppos(actual O|pos)
models.secondaryGain: log2 Psel(actual O|S0,pos) - log2 Pglobal(actual O)

counterfactual.substitute: for each frozen eligible operator, choose the distinct eligible operator with closest TRAIN global support; ties lexical

null.description: For each position bucket, permute frozen TRAIN state-conditioned selection residual blocks across supported anonymous states, preserving Ppos, operator vocabulary, state support, position support, and residual magnitudes while breaking the actual state-to-selection mapping.

evaluation.primaryGate: operator-balanced primary gain > 0; residual-reassignment p at threshold; >=60% evaluable operators positive; counterfactual actual-over-substitute preference > 0.50; sufficient support; BOTH holdout and control
evaluation.operatorBalance: average event gain within operator, then equally across evaluable operators

crossSystem.profile: for each anonymous state with sufficient sealed support in both systems, compute mean primary selection gain across eligible events; correlate Hebrew and glyph state profiles
crossSystem.replicationRule: same-sign positive Pearson correlation with p<=.05 in BOTH holdout and control for a Hebrew representation
